An international choral festival

Cantapueblo is an international choral gathering that promotes friendship, cooperation and understanding between peoples through choral singing. Every edition brings together children's, youth, adult, professional and amateur choirs, in theaters, churches, cultural centers and open-air venues across Mendoza — from Plaza Independencia to the foot of Cerro Aconcagua.

What we're after

Widening our horizon. We're the choral festival most chosen by our Latin American peers — four continents are still left to explore.

What we do

We work as a team — there's synergy, and it shows in the sum of it. We have fun, because Cantapueblo is exactly that, a choral feast, and that's how we live it. We make friends, and our friends always come back to the place where they were happy.

What sets us apart

Leading choral activity in Argentina. Pioneers in Latin America and the world. More than 35 years of history. A quality service, always.

El Canto Grande

In 1990, Gloria Brastchi and Alejandro Scarpetta wrote Cantapueblo's official song. Over more than 30 years, it has been performed by thousands of choirs who passed through this festival.

Singing at our festival is an experience you will never forget. The emotion runs high in every concert. Your choir, the beautiful landscapes, good wine and the warmth of our people are the perfect alchemy to celebrate life at Cantapueblo.

Alejandro Scarpetta — Founder and Artistic Director

Recognized in the choral world

Regional leadership

A benchmark for choral activity in Argentina, and one of Latin America's most-attended choral festivals.

UNESCO recognition

Named a "Landmark Event for the Culture of Peace" by UNESCO in the year 2000.

International reach

Choirs from more than twenty countries have taken part across the festival's editions.
